decision.summary: Compressed perceptual narrative is the strongest reviewed direction, but it should remain lab-first or explicitly opt-in until tested on a larger paired corpus.

version_winners.why: Keeps product-first hierarchy and restraint/density tension while reducing methodological scaffolding.
version_winners.residual_risk: Institutional authority must remain a possible reading, not a fact.

version_winners.why: Retains obstruction and copy-supported limits while sounding sharper than the raw version.
version_winners.residual_risk: Product UX clarity must not become fact without product-surface evidence.

version_winners.why: Keeps operational density and complexity/guidance tension with little overreach risk.
version_winners.residual_risk: Low, if visible docs evidence exists.

version_winners.why: Improves flow while preserving explicit mental-health caution.
version_winners.residual_risk: Caution must remain visible around support, therapy, wellness, and user outcomes.

version_winners.why: Turns weak evidence into bounded absence without punitive baseline language.
version_winners.residual_risk: Compression can become too blunt if limits around strategic failure are removed.

where_compression_improves_flow: Starts with observable surface behavior instead of method commentary.
Turns long confidence explanations into compact evidence limits.
Makes productive tension easier to read.
Removes phrases such as supports a high-confidence observation and the narrative should name.
Reduces generic quality adjectives such as premium, modern, robust, developer-friendly, and refined.

where_compression_loses_caution.risk: Possible readings can become factual strategic claims if boundary clauses disappear.
Compressed warmth language can imply user support or therapeutic impact.
Absence can become blunt verdict if the caveat around strategic failure is omitted.

where_baseline_remains_safer: When evidence is too thin and the user only needs a plain summary.
When there are not enough captures or source observations to anchor perceptual language.
When the brand category is sensitive and explicit caution cannot be preserved.
When perceptual pattern vocabulary would be introduced without case-specific evidence.

remaining_overreach_risks.description: Compression must not turn possible reading into the brand seeks.
Wellness, trust, support, clarity, and developer success cannot be asserted from surface tone or copy alone.
Interface clarity and workflow effectiveness must remain copy-supported unless direct product evidence exists.
Product polish, restraint, or density must not become premium, sophisticated, or leader language.
Weak brands should be described through low specificity and weak corroboration, not strategic failure.

why: Evidence-bound without sounding like methodology notes.
Keeps interpretation conditional without over-explaining the condition.
Privileges surface behavior over reputation and quality labels.
Names productive tensions in compact language.

minimum_conditions: Compression only runs after perceptual hints or augmented findings exist.
Low-confidence and copy-supported material must retain explicit caution.
Sensitive categories must keep visible limitations.
The system must preserve at least one evidence mechanism per compressed finding.
Human comparison remains available before production rollout.

final_judgment: Compressed perceptual narrative is the best current direction for Brand3/FLOC* report voice. It keeps the epistemology but removes the self-consciousness.
